title: Working with Arrow and Parquet
text: A5 cell IDs 64-bit unsigned integers. R native uint64 type, double can represent integers exactly 2^53. Nearly half A5 cell IDs exceed threshold, converting double silently corrupts data. problem reading Parquet files store A5 cell IDs uint64 columns: standard format used DuckDB, Python, geoparquet.io. default, arrow::read_parquet() converts uint64 R’s double, losing precision:
code: library(arrow) library(tibble) library(a5R)  # A real A5 cell: Edinburgh at resolution 20 cell <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 20) a5_u64_to_hex(cell) #> [1] "63bb93f88f080000"  # Write to Parquet as uint64 (the standard interchange format) tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet") arrow::write_parquet(   arrow::arrow_table(cell_id = a5_cell_to_arrow(cell)),   tf )  # Read it back naively: arrow silently converts uint64 to double (naive <- tibble(arrow::read_parquet(tf))) #> # A tibble: 1 × 1 #>   cell_id #>     <dbl> #> 1 7.19e18  cell_as_dbl <- naive$cell_id  # The double can't distinguish this cell from nearby IDs cell_as_dbl == cell_as_dbl + 1   # TRUE: silent corruption #> [1] TRUE cell_as_dbl == cell_as_dbl + 100 # still TRUE #> [1] TRUE

text: A5 cell ID 64-bit unsigned integer (u64). R native u64 type: integers 32-bit signed (-2^31 2^31 - 1), doubles 64-bit floating point. double can represent integers exactly 2^53, u64 can go 2^64 - 1. obvious workaround store cell IDs hex strings ("0800000000000006"). works, every trip across R / Rust boundary requires hex parsing formatting: O(n) string allocation dominates cost lightweight operations like a5_get_resolution() a5_cell_to_parent().

title: How a5R stores cell IDs without strings
text: u64 exactly 8 bytes. store byte little-endian representation separate raw vector field vctrs record type, one twist: significant byte, b8, stored XOR 0xFC (see NA handling ). lossless: XOR constant inverse, eight stored bytes map one--one onto original u64. Rust side, reconstructing id eight byte slices one XOR single u64::from_le_bytes() call. pointers, a5_cell can saved saveRDS() like R object. Objects saved a5R 0.6.0 earlier used plain byte layout read correctly later versions; re-create hex strings Arrow, store true id.

title: How a5R stores cell IDs without strings
text: R side, a5_cell vctrs record (vctrs::new_rcrd()) eight fields (b1 b8): field plain raw vector: contiguous block memory per-element overhead. Subsetting, combining, NA propagation handled automatically vctrs. Hex strings produced demand:
code: library(a5R) cell <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 10) vctrs::field(cell, "b1") #> [1] 00 vctrs::field(cell, "b8") # stored XOR 0xFC #> [1] 9f # Display calls format(), which converts to hex for readability cell #> <a5_cell[1]> #> [1] 63bb948000000000  # Explicit conversion a5_u64_to_hex(cell) #> [1] "63bb948000000000"  # Round-trip from hex a5_cell("0800000000000006") #> <a5_cell[1]> #> [1] 0800000000000006

Resolution 30 keeps just 5, 3 1 quintant bits top make room position bits, valid resolution-30 cells can top byte 0xFC. Storing b8 XOR 0xFC makes sentinel’s stored form eight 00 bytes. matters vctrs fills gaps field field, missing raw value 00. Combining NA, subsetting NA index, assigning NA, unmatched rows joins produce eight 00 bytes, decode NA. plain bytes decode id 0, world cell, valid id. Rust side, sentinel detected mapped None. Base classes behave way: c(NA, Sys.Date()) loses Date class. Start cell, c(a5_cell(NA), cells), use vctrs::vec_c(NA, cells), combines every argument’s type. text: a5_covering holds one compacted set cells per element, uses different layout. element single raw vector covering’s 64-bit values, little-endian unmasked: cells sorted curve order, compaction marker, exactly A5 libraries return . Rust reads element one slice, Arrow export one list<uint64> value per covering. compaction marker value cell can take: quintant 60 (0 59 exist) top 6 bits, resolution bits 55 48, tag 1000000 low 7 bits, resolution uses. marker resolution 12 0xf00c000000000040: covering never holds NA, byte masked. missing covering NULL element, vctrs fills list, joins vec_init() produce NA coverings extra work.
code: covering <- a5_compact(a5_cell_to_children(cell, resolution = 12)) covering #> <a5_covering[1]> #> [1] res 12: 16 cells (1 stored) bytes <- unclass(covering)[[1]] length(bytes) / 8                 # one stored cell, then the marker #> [1] 2 rev(bytes[9:16])                  # the marker, most significant byte first #> [1] f0 0c 00 00 00 00 00 40

title: Multi-threading
text: can also set threads package load time via R option environment variable, useful scripts batch jobs: a5_set_threads() invisibly returns previous value, making temporary changes easy:
code: # Check the current setting (default: 1) a5_get_threads() #> [1] 1  # Use 4 threads a5_set_threads(4) a5_get_threads() #> [1] 4 # In .Rprofile or at the top of a script options(a5R.threads = 4)  # Or as an environment variable # Sys.setenv(A5R_NUM_THREADS = 4) old <- a5_set_threads(4) # ... parallel work ... a5_set_threads(old)

title: Multi-threading
text: Threading applies vectorised functions process element independently: one--many functions (a5_grid_disk(), a5_spherical_cap(), a5_cell_to_children(), a5_uncompact()) per-element work parallelised; assembling result, especially simplify = FALSE list, sequential, list form gains less flat form. Scalar bulk operations (a5_compact(), a5_cell_area(), a5_cell_child(), a5_cell_children_range(), etc.) unaffected: already fast delegate algorithms don’t parallelise element-wise.

title: Multi-threading
text: Threading small fixed overhead (thread synchronisation, memory allocation intermediate results). small vectors can outweigh benefit. rule thumb: < 1,000 elements: stick 1 thread 1,000–10,000: 2-4 threads helps heavy ops (boundary, indexing) > 10,000: use many threads cores ’s quick comparison 100k cells: Note user time increases (total CPU work across threads) elapsed (wall-clock) time decreases: parallelism work.
code: cells <- a5_uncompact(a5_polygon_to_cells(wk::rct(-10, 50, 10, 60), resolution = 12)) length(cells) #> [1] 704259  a5_set_threads(1) system.time(a5_cell_to_boundary(cells, format = "wkt")) #>   user  system elapsed #>  3.124   0.000   3.122   a5_set_threads(8) system.time(a5_cell_to_boundary(cells, format = "wkt")) #>   user  system elapsed #> 6.195   1.289   1.667

title: Multi-threading
text: a5R uses dedicated rayon thread pool, separate R’s parallelism. safe use alongside future, mirai, etc. think carefully nested parallelism can, overloaded, degrade performance. thread pool rebuilt time call a5_set_threads(), changing count mid-session fine (cheap) free: ideally, start workflow rather toggling per-call.

title: Moving between resolutions by location
text: a5_cell_to_parent() a5_cell_to_children() follow A5 index. cell’s index children tile : lie mostly neighbours, cells inside belong neighbour’s index. a5_cell_to_supercell() a5_cell_to_subcell() follow location instead. fine cell belongs coarse cell containing centre: coarse cell supercell, fine cells coarse cell holds subcells.  cell 64 index children 66 subcells , subcells sit inside outline. mismatch rare: third res-18 cells, index parent res 15 neighbour cell lie , supercell. upward direction shows thing side. one res-10 cell whose index parent res 8 cell lies :  fine cell (dark, centre white) sits inside supercell, index parent neighbouring cell.
code: cell <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-53.5, -19, resolution = 8) index_kids <- a5_cell_to_children(cell, resolution = 11) spatial_kids <- a5_uncompact(a5_cell_to_subcell(cell, resolution = 11))  outline <- a5_cell_to_boundary(cell) lim <- wk::wk_bbox(a5_cell_to_boundary(c(index_kids, spatial_kids))) lim <- unclass(lim)  for (panel in list(list(index_kids, "Index children"),                    list(spatial_kids, "Subcells"))) {   plot(NULL, xlim = c(lim$xmin, lim$xmax), ylim = c(lim$ymin, lim$ymax),        asp = 1, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", main = panel[[2]])   plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(panel[[1]]), col = "#206ead40",        border = "#206ead", add = TRUE)   plot(outline, border = "#333333", lwd = 2, add = TRUE) } set.seed(1) fine <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(   stats::runif(1e4, -54, -53), stats::runif(1e4, -19.5, -18.5),   resolution = 18 ) mean(a5_cell_to_parent(fine, 15) != a5_cell_to_supercell(fine, 15)) #> [1] 0.3677 kids <- a5_uncompact(a5_grid_disk(cell, 1), resolution = 10) moved <- kids[a5_cell_to_parent(kids, 8) != a5_cell_to_supercell(kids, 8)] # the clearest case: the fine cell furthest from its index parent's centre fine_cell <- moved[which.max(a5_cell_distance(moved, a5_cell_to_parent(moved, 8)))] index_parent <- a5_cell_to_parent(fine_cell, 8) supercell <- a5_cell_to_supercell(fine_cell, 8)  lim <- unclass(wk::wk_bbox(a5_cell_to_boundary(c(index_parent, supercell))))  plot(NULL, xlim = c(lim$xmin, lim$xmax), ylim = c(lim$ymin, lim$ymax),      asp = 1, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "") plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(index_parent), col = "#d9534f20", border = "#d9534f",      lwd = 2, lty = 2, add = TRUE) plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(supercell), col = "#206ead20", border = "#206ead",      lwd = 2, add = TRUE) plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(fine_cell), col = "#333333", border = NA, add = TRUE) plot(a5_cell_to_lonlat(fine_cell), pch = 19, cex = 0.8, col = "white", add = TRUE) legend("bottomright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, lty = c(2, 1),        col = c("#d9534f", "#206ead"), legend = c("Index parent", "Supercell"))

Average res 15 rule. reference uses neither hierarchy, drop two million random points area, place directly res-15 cell, take share points per cell fall patch. estimates coarse cell’s true patch fraction. Aggregating index parent misstates patch fraction cells touches tenth average, third worst, coarse cell averages fine cells neighbours. Aggregating supercell sampling noise reference. format() supplies grouping key base grouping functions group a5_cell vector directly (see vignette("internal-cell-representation")). code: area <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-53.5, -19, resolution = 12) layer <- a5_uncompact(a5_grid_disk(area, 1), resolution = 18) length(layer) #> [1] 24576  centre <- unclass(a5_cell_to_lonlat(area)) in_patch <- function(p) {   p <- unclass(p)   as.numeric((p$x - centre$x)^2 + (p$y - centre$y)^2 < 0.004^2) } fine <- data.frame(value = in_patch(a5_cell_to_lonlat(layer)))  mean_by <- function(cell, value) {   stats::aggregate(list(value = value), list(cell = format(cell)), mean) } by_index <- mean_by(a5_cell_to_parent(layer, 15), fine$value) by_super <- mean_by(a5_cell_to_supercell(layer, 15), fine$value) set.seed(1) bb <- unclass(wk::wk_bbox(a5_cell_to_lonlat(layer))) pts <- list(x = stats::runif(2e6, bb$xmin, bb$xmax),             y = stats::runif(2e6, bb$ymin, bb$ymax)) truth <- mean_by(a5_lonlat_to_cell(pts$x, pts$y, resolution = 15), in_patch(pts)) names(truth)[2] <- "truth"  error <- function(agg) {   m <- merge(agg, truth)   m <- m[m$value > 0 | m$truth > 0, ]   round(c(mean = mean(abs(m$value - m$truth)), max = max(abs(m$value - m$truth))), 3) } error(by_index) #>  mean   max  #> 0.086 0.338 error(by_super) #>  mean   max  #> 0.008 0.057 grid <- merge(merge(truth, by_index, all.x = TRUE), by_super,               by = "cell", all.x = TRUE, suffixes = c("_index", "_super")) grid[is.na(grid)] <- 0 cells <- a5_cell(grid$cell) xy <- unclass(a5_cell_to_lonlat(cells)) near <- (xy$x - centre$x)^2 + (xy$y - centre$y)^2 < 0.006^2 grid <- grid[near, ] boundaries <- a5_cell_to_boundary(cells[near]) lim <- unclass(wk::wk_bbox(boundaries))  fraction_pal <- hcl.colors(101, "Greens", rev = TRUE) error_pal <- hcl.colors(101, "Blue-Red 3") ring <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200) error_col <- function(e) error_pal[round(pmin(pmax(e / 0.4, -1), 1) * 50) + 51]  for (panel in list(   list(fraction_pal[round(grid$truth * 100) + 1], "Reference fraction"),   list(error_col(grid$value_index - grid$truth), "Index parent error"),   list(error_col(grid$value_super - grid$truth), "Supercell error") )) {   plot(NULL, xlim = c(lim$xmin, lim$xmax), ylim = c(lim$ymin, lim$ymax),        asp = 1, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", main = panel[[2]])   plot(boundaries, col = panel[[1]], border = "white", lwd = 0.5, add = TRUE)   lines(centre$x + 0.004 * cos(ring), centre$y + 0.004 * sin(ring),         col = "#333333", lwd = 1.5) }

title: Traversal and distance
text: Pick origin cell use a5_spherical_cap() grab every cell whose centre falls within given great-circle radius. Like a5_grid_disk(), returns a5_covering: compacted set records resolution. Pass a5_uncompact() cells. a5_grid_disk() selects cells hop count rather metric distance. vertex = FALSE (default) edge-sharing neighbours traversed (4-connected), producing diamond shape. Setting vertex = TRUE includes corner-sharing neighbours (8-connected), giving squarer footprint.
code: origin <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(35, 55, resolution = 14)  a5_spherical_cap(origin, radius = 5000) #> <a5_covering[1]> #> [1] res 14: 621 cells (105 stored)  disk <- a5_uncompact(a5_grid_disk(origin, k = 20, vertex = FALSE)) disk_vertex <- a5_uncompact(a5_grid_disk(origin, k = 20, vertex = TRUE)) cap <- a5_uncompact(a5_spherical_cap(origin, radius = 5000))

title: Traversal and distance
text: Compute distance origin every cell cap (disk) visualise colour gradient.  Distance radiates smoothly centre. Cells near origin dark, cells rim bright. origin cell shown white border reference.
code: dcap <- a5_cell_distance(origin, cap, units = "km") ddisk <- a5_cell_distance(origin, disk, units = "km") ddisk_vertex <- a5_cell_distance(origin, disk_vertex, units = "km")  pal <- hcl.colors(256, "Inferno")  for (info in list(   list(s = disk, d = ddisk, lab = "Grid disk (edges)"),   list(s = disk_vertex, d = ddisk_vertex, lab = "Grid disk (vertices)"),   list(s = cap, d = dcap, lab = "Spherical cap") )) {   brk <- seq(0, max(as.numeric(info$d)), length.out = 257)   cols <- pal[findInterval(as.numeric(info$d), brk, all.inside = TRUE)]    plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(info$s), col = cols, border = NA, asp = 1,        main = info$lab)   plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(origin), border = "#ffffffff", add = TRUE) }

title: Traversal and distance
text: a5R supports three distance methods: haversine (great-circle), geodesic (WGS84 ellipsoid via Karney 2013), rhumb (loxodrome / constant-bearing). short distances nearly identical; differences grow distance.  difference near zero centre grows ~1675 m rim (~500 km away).
code: wide_origin <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(35, 55, resolution = 8) wide_cap <- a5_uncompact(a5_spherical_cap(wide_origin, radius = 500000))  hav <- a5_cell_distance(wide_origin, wide_cap, units = "m", method = "haversine") geo <- a5_cell_distance(wide_origin, wide_cap, units = "m", method = "geodesic")  diff_m <- as.numeric(geo - hav) brk <- seq(min(diff_m), max(diff_m), length.out = 257) cols <- pal[findInterval(diff_m, brk, all.inside = TRUE)]  layout(matrix(c(1, 2), nrow = 1), widths = c(4, 1)) par(mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1)) plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(wide_cap), col = cols, border = NA, asp = 1,      main = "Geodesic \u2212 Haversine (m)")  par(mar = c(9, 0, 9, 9)) image(1, seq(min(diff_m), max(diff_m), length.out = 256),       t(seq_along(pal)), col = pal, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "") axis(4, las = 1)

Dropped lifecycle R dependency wkt Rust dependency, needed a5_grid(). Replaced heavy geo Rust dependency lightweight geographiclib-rs crate a5_cell_distance(). haversine rhumb methods now computed directly; geodesic method continues use Karney’s algorithm. Distance results unchanged. removes 33 transitive crates shrinks vendored sources substantially. Results unchanged; implementation simpler avoids uncompact/recompact round-trip single-part polygons.

title: a5R 0.4.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-05-14 a5_grid() soft-deprecated favour a5_polygon_to_cells(). New a5_polygon_to_cells() returns A5 cells whose centres lie inside polygon. Distinct a5_grid(), uses boundary-intersection semantics. Accepts wk-handleable geometries (including MULTIPOLYGON sfc several polygons), terra SpatVector objects, numeric matrices, data.frame(lon, lat). Multi-part inputs handled natively: per polygon part outer ring’s cells computed hole-ring cells subtracted, results unioned across parts recompacted. New a5_linestring_to_cells() returns A5 cells whose pentagons intersected great-circle polyline, discovery order along path. Accepts input shapes a5_polygon_to_cells(), including MULTILINESTRING, sfcs multiple linestrings, terra SpatVector objects; per-feature outputs concatenated first-seen deduplication.
